bodies.name: Albion
bodies.axesStatus: Illustrative equal axes at a diameter estimated from brightness with an assumed albedo of 0.14; not measured.
bodies.credit: JPL Small-Body Database absolute magnitude H = 7.18 for 15760 Albion (1992 QB1); diameter estimated by cssEarth with the 0.14 median albedo of cold classical objects from Vilenius et al. (2014), Astronomy & Astrophysics 564, A35
bodies.shapeMeaning: Illustrative sphere at 130.2 km, estimated from JPL's absolute magnitude H = 7.18 with an assumed albedo of 0.14, the median Vilenius et al. (2014) report for cold classical objects. The size is not measured.
bodies.orientationMeaning: Illustrative ICRF north pole, arbitrary prime meridian and phase; no spin pole is published.
bodies.surfaceMeaning: Unmapped surface: the standard grid is a coordinate aid, not observed colour or terrain.
bodies.introduction: Albion, found in 1992 as 1992 QB1, was the first Kuiper belt object discovered after Pluto and Charon.
bodies.card: The first Kuiper belt object found after Pluto.
bodies.datasetSummary: A sphere at about 130.2 km, estimated from brightness with an assumed albedo.

bodies.name: Uni
bodies.axesStatus: Illustrative equal axes at the radiometric diameter; not three measured axes.
bodies.credit: Fornasier et al. (2013), Astronomy & Astrophysics 555, A15; Herschel PACS and SPIRE thermal radiometry
bodies.shapeMeaning: Illustrative sphere at the 692 ± 23 km diameter measured from thermal emission. No shape model is published.
bodies.orientationMeaning: Illustrative ICRF north pole, arbitrary prime meridian and phase; no spin pole is published.
bodies.surfaceMeaning: Unmapped surface: the standard grid is a coordinate aid, not observed colour or terrain.
bodies.introduction: Uni is a large icy body in the Kuiper belt beyond Neptune, first catalogued as 2002 UX25.
bodies.card: A large icy body in the Kuiper belt.
bodies.datasetSummary: A sphere at the 692 km diameter measured from its heat. Shape and pole are not measured.
